text: White tip disease (ជំងឺចុងសលឹកស) is caused by the nematode Aphelenchoides besseyi, and can cause yield losses of roughly 10–50%. It tends to be worse in cooler areas than in fully tropical zones. Symptoms: the tip of the leaf turns white — noticeably whiter than the pale color of a normally aging leaf. Infected plants are stunted, tiller poorly, and produce small panicles with few, small, malformed grains. The nematode starts out in the young, still-rolled leaf near the growing tip. It travels either along the surface of the plant or is carried by water into the plant's inner tissue; once it has built up in numbers there, it damages the developing panicle. It can also survive inside the grain husk or on the surface of infected grain, which is how it carries over to the next planting. Management: (1) clean seed before planting by soaking it in hot water (roughly 52–53°C) for 15 minutes to kill the nematode; (2) planting the early/wet season crop, rather than late season, can reduce how much the disease shows up.
